text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar –  10 To ask the Minister for Transport whether there are plans to make it a requirement for bicycle-sharing companies to collectively invest in and construct bicycle docking stations, particularly around housing estates, to mitigate the current problem of having their shared bicycles strewn around untidily or causing obstruction.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether enforcement action will be taken against hirers of rental bicycles who dump the bicycles in an indiscriminate manner.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the geo-fencing and incentive/disincentive elements in the bike-sharing operators' mobile applications have addressed the indiscriminate parking of bicycles; (b) what more can be done to compel the operators to make more investments to unilaterally clear indiscriminately parked bicycles expeditiously; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider subsidising agencies, such as Town Councils and commercial establishments, to remove or report such bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has been working with the other agencies to provide more parking spaces and step up enforcement.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In October 2017, LTA, the National Parks Board (NParks) and Town Councils signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with BSOs, which sets out guidelines on the responsible operation of bicycle-sharing services in public spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As part of the proposed licensing framework, BSOs will be required to remove indiscriminately parked bicycles on public land within a stipulated time period.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: BSOs will also be required to adopt schemes that will disincentivise users for indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: More details of the licensing framework will be announced when ready.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If we fine litterbugs from throwing cigarette butts, why should we not fine bicycle users for throwing their bicycles on the roadside, or expressways, flyovers, drains?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They create such an eyesore for members of the public, so the entire public is put to inconvenience because of the indiscriminate littering of bicycles by some inconsiderate users.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA currently adopts a five-pronged approach to managing disamenities of dockless bicycle sharing.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: First, we are providing more public bicycle parking spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has been working with the BSOs to educate shared bicycle users, and we have developed educational materials on proper bicycle etiquette.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Some BSOs have implemented GPS geo-fencing, and users that park bicycles within a geo-fenced parking zone are given incentives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There are also BSOs which have implemented Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) geo stations and charge a towing fee to users who do not park properly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Fourthly, of course, we do step up enforcement actions.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Currently, what we do is to fine a BSO which fails to retrieve indiscriminately parked bicycles.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Next, like I had mentioned in my reply, we did sign an MOU together with the BSOs, NParks and Town Councils.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The MOU aims to encourage responsible operation of bike-sharing services in public spaces.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to penalising users, under the current Street Works Act, users who indiscriminately park their bicycles on public streets and cause obstruction and inconvenience can be fined up to $2,000.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It is difficult to catch users in the act of parking bicycles indiscriminately.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can I just check how many times have each of the BSOs been issued fines for neglecting the shared bicycles that are strewn all over the place, and are there plans to tighten this penalty mechanism imposed on the BSOs?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Based on the number of notices issued and bicycles impounded from the period May 2017 to 21 January 2018, there was a total of 2,171 removal notices issued, and the number of bicycles impounded adds up to 341.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The total fines collected by LTA amounted to about $180,000.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: These do not include those issued by the Town Councils or NParks.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I would like a bit more information on this licensing regime that the Minister spoke about.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because it does appear that in spite of these fines that have been given to the BSOs, there is still a long way to go in terms of ensuring that the bicycles are not causing disamenity to members of the public.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State is there a regime which LTA imposes on the BSOs to clear bicycles expeditiously?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think there is currently a four-hour timeline where they have to remove the bicycles.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: However, many of them still cannot make that timeline.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In relation to my Parliamentary Question, even though Town Councils have signed the MOU with LTA, the reality is Town Council officers or property officers do not have that much leeway of time to go around looking for these bicycles and then monitoring whether they are cleared within four hours or not.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Is LTA going to look at the prospect of requiring the BSOs to intensify their efforts to pick up illegally or indiscriminately parked bikes?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I will be sharing more of this when it is ready.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I think part of the issue is about the demand and supply, probably because of the cost of the bicycle.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How is LTA monitoring and managing this with the BSOs in terms of the growth rate with which they are putting the bicycles out?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA does have regular meetings with BSOs to discuss issues relating to their daily operations as well as the problem of indiscriminate parking.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, when we do propose the legislative amendments, this will set out the regulatory framework, the licensing framework, to control the operations of the BSOs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State assure the House and residents affected that in this study of the upcoming framework, his Ministry will study expedited requirements to remove a bicycle, especially in areas where access is critical?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will be consulting the stakeholders as well as the industry.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And we will keep all these in mind during the discussion.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I wanted to ask the Senior Minister of State why are we just focusing on giving fines to the BSOs?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Surely, the BSOs should be able to review the data of the last user of the bicycle who left his bicycle in an indiscriminate manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Would the Senior of State not agree with me that we would be better able to shape user behaviour if we impose a fine on those users who park their bicycles in a manner that obstruct fire exits and wheelchair ramps?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I would just like to remind all Members of the House that while there may be interim inconveniences and disamenities, I would like to reiterate that there are actually many benefits of the bike-sharing scheme, not just the disamenities that we are currently facing, which may be transient in nature.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Benefits include transport flexibility in terms of first- and last-mile connectivity.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There will be reductions in vehicle emissions if we are able to bring the population of car ownership down.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to that, there are also health benefits of cycling.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: It will also reduce congestion and fuel consumption.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: More importantly, it complements our vision of a car-lite society.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I was particularly thrilled by a column that I read yesterday, an opinion of the day by one of our young journalists in The Straits Times.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: She shared her initial apprehension and scepticism of the bike-sharing scheme but later found the experience pleasing and enjoyable, and I would like to quote her: "When the bike-sharing scheme started in Singapore about a year ago, some turned up their noses at this new sharing economy service and doubted it would last.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: After all, photos of bikes upended in the middle of a desolated field or abandoned in the storm drain triggered widespread outrage.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But writing here as a car-less commuter who often feels defeated by the merciless crush of people on public transport, I am all for bike-sharing as it has given commuting a new lease of life and transformed the way I experience my city." So, I would like to urge all Members of the House and fellow Singaporeans to give the bike-sharing scheme a chance to evolve into a safe and convenient mode of transport in our daily lives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, for this to become a reality, we need the support of everyone ‒ the authorities, the BSOs and, more importantly, you, the users of the bike-sharing scheme.
